interview:
A1: The running count is rendered into the existing success area (#form-result) as part of the success message. After a successful submit the page shows something like 'Message ready — your mail client should open to send it. You have sent N messages on this device.' where N comes from localStorage and increments on each successful submit. The count must survive reload.

A2: Persistence uses localStorage only: read the stored count on load (defaulting to 0 when absent), and write the incremented count back on each successful submit. No cookies, no server, no storage library.

A3: Visit availability is a small data file `data/schedule.js` that assigns a plain JavaScript array of visit slots (or office-hours strings) to a global variable. The page includes it with an ordinary <script src="data/schedule.js"></script> tag placed before script.js, and script.js reads the global to render the first available slot (or the hours) as a short line inside the About section. This is what makes the page work over file:// — no fetch, no XMLHttpRequest.

A4: The only files that may change are index.html and script.js, and one new file data/schedule.js must be created. Do not create any other new file, do not add a build step or dependency, do not modify .factory/ or factory.yaml, and do not touch the tests/ directory.

A5: Every existing behavior must keep working: the five-section navigation with show/hide, the contact form field ids (contact-name, contact-email, contact-message), validation (empty name/email/message, invalid email), the mailto action, and the footer year. No CSS of any kind is allowed.
